summary: Check the Neural Networks (Elsevier) Guide for Authors in detail

checks.findings:
SOURCE NOTE: www.sciencedirect.com returns HTTP 403 to plain fetches, so the Guide for Authors was read in a real browser session (full rendered text of https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/neural-networks/publish/guide-for-authors, retrieved 11 Aug 2026). All quotes below are verbatim from that page unless another URL is named. Linked Elsevier policy pages were fetched separately.

FACTUAL CORRECTION TO THE TASK PREMISE: the current guide does NOT list ENNS. It says: "Neural Networks is the archival journal of three of the oldest and most prominent neural network societies: the International Neural Network Society (INNS), the Asia-Pacific Neural Network Society (APNNS), and the Japanese Neural Network Society (JNNS)." ISSN 0893-6080 is correct.

=====================================================================
1. PEER REVIEW MODEL — SINGLE ANONYMIZED. AUTHOR NAMES ARE INCLUDED.
=====================================================================
Verbatim (Guide, "Peer review"):
"This journal follows a single anonymized review process. Your submission will initially be assessed by our editors to determine suitability for publication in this journal. If your submission is deemed suitable, it will typically be sent to be reviewed by a minimum of two reviewers for an independent expert assessment of the scientific quality. The decision as to whether your article is accepted or rejected will be made by our editors."

Elsevier's definition of that model (https://www.elsevier.com/reviewer/what-is-peer-review):
- Single anonymized: "In this type of review, the names of the reviewers are hidden from the author."
- Double anonymized: "Both the reviewer and the author are anonymous in this model."

=> CONSEQUENCE: Neural Networks is single-anonymized/single-blind. Reviewers see the authors; authors do not see reviewers. Author names, affiliations and acknowledgements MUST be included in the submitted manuscript. There is NO anonymization requirement, no blinded version, and no instruction to strip identifying information. (Do NOT use elsarticle's `doubleblind` option.)

Corroborating: the "Title page" section requires full author names, affiliations, postal addresses, country, emails and a designated corresponding author in the manuscript itself: "You are required to include the following details in the title page information: Article title... Author names. Provide the given name(s) and family name(s) of each author. The order of authors should match the order in the submission system... Affiliations, referring to where the work was carried out, below the author names... Ensure that you provide the full name and postal address of each affiliation, including the country name and, if available, the email address of each author... Corresponding author."

Appeals: "Authors may submit a formal appeal request to the editorial decision, provided it meets all the requirements and follows the procedure outlined in Elsevier's Appeal Policy. Only one appeal per submission will be considered and the appeal decision will be final."

=====================================================================
2. ARTICLE TYPES AND LENGTH LIMITS
=====================================================================
Four types are defined. KEY POINT: there is NO stated page or word limit for a full/regular research Article — the only length limits in the guide apply to Letters and Letters to the Editor.

(a) ARTICLES (the full/regular research paper) — verbatim:
"Original, full-length articles are considered with the understanding that they have not been published except in abstract form and are not concurrently under review elsewhere. Authors need to specify one of the five Sections: Cognitive Science, Neuroscience, Learning Systems, Mathematical and Computational Analysis, Engineering and Applications."
=> No word count, no page count, no reference cap is stated. The mandatory extra step is selecting one of the five Sections at submission.

(b) LETTERS — verbatim:
"Letters (up to 2500 words) are expected to contain important new research results for which rapid publication is justified. Each Letter should include an abstract (no more than 100 words), and a maximum of 25 references. Figures and tables together with their legends should occupy no more than one of the pages.
A Letter submission undergoes an expedited review cycle, and a major revision is not allowed. If a submission requires a substantial revision, the authors are encouraged to resubmit a revised version as an Article."

(c) REVIEWS OR TUTORIALS — verbatim:
"Topical, comprehensive reviews that summarize significant advances in a broad area of research, or tutorials that provide an introduction to such advances. Authors must contact the Review Editor with a review/tutorial outline before submitting the full manuscript."
=> Pre-submission contact with the Review Editor is MANDATORY for this type.

(d) LETTERS TO THE EDITOR — verbatim:
"Short communications that comment on, point out errors in, or express a significant disagreement with a previously published paper in this journal. An author of the original paper will be asked to review the submission along with independent reviewers. In the case of substantive disagreement between the authors of a Letter to the Editor and the authors of the original paper, the Editor may invite to a rebuttal from the latter authors. Such letters should be as concise as possible, not exceeding 2 formatted pages. If both the Letter to the Editor and the Rebuttal are accepted, they will be published in the same issue."

Also stated (Aims and scope): "The journal publishes articles, letters, and reviews/tutorials, as well as letters to the editor, editorials, and current events."

Conference-paper extension policy (verbatim, under "Submission checklist"), which is journal-specific and often missed:
"Policy Regarding Prior Conference Papers and Rejected Manuscripts
It is acceptable for conference papers to be extended to a journal submission. However, authors are required to cite their related prior work and the extension must be substantial, such as new experimental results or analyses. The journal submission should clearly specify how the journal paper differs from or goes beyond the cited prior work."

=====================================================================
3. ABSTRACT
=====================================================================
Verbatim:
"You are required to provide a concise and factual abstract which does not exceed 250 words. The abstract should briefly state the purpose of your research, principal results and major conclusions. Some guidelines:
Abstracts must be able to stand alone as abstracts are often presented separately from the article.
Avoid references. If any are essential to include, ensure that you cite the author(s) and year(s).
Avoid non-standard or uncommon abbreviations. If any are essential to include, ensure they are defined within your abstract at first mention."

=> Limit: 250 words maximum (100 words for Letters).
=> UNSTRUCTURED. No structured-abstract headings (Background/Methods/Results) are required or mentioned anywhere.
=> References: discouraged but not absolutely banned ("Avoid references"); if essential, cite author(s) and year(s). Additionally, under "References within text": "References cited in your abstract must be given in full."
=> Abbreviations: avoid non-standard/uncommon ones; define at first mention if essential.
=> The abstract is excluded from section numbering: "Do not include the article abstract within section numbering."

=====================================================================
4. KEYWORDS — 1 TO 6
=====================================================================
Verbatim:
"You are required to provide 1 to 6 keywords for indexing purposes. Keywords should be written in English. Please try to avoid keywords consisting of multiple words (using "and" or "of").
We recommend that you only use abbreviations in keywords if they are firmly established in the field."

=====================================================================
5. HIGHLIGHTS — OPTIONAL (ENCOURAGED), NOT REQUIRED
=====================================================================
Verbatim:
"You are encouraged to provide article highlights at submission.
Highlights are a short collection of bullet points that should capture the novel results of your research as well as any new methods used during your study. Highlights will help increase the discoverability of your article via search engines. Some guidelines:
Submit highlights as a separate editable file in the online submission system with the word "highlights" included in the file name.
Highlights should consist of 3 to 5 bullet points, each a maximum of 85 characters, including spaces.
We encourage you to view example article highlights and read about the benefits of their inclusion."

Exact rules: 3 to 5 bullet points; each bullet max 85 characters INCLUDING SPACES; separate editable file (not embedded in the manuscript); filename must contain the word "highlights".

Elsevier's Highlights page (https://www.elsevier.com/researcher/author/tools-and-resources/highlights) adds: "three to five (three to four for Cell Press articles)"; "Each Highlight can be no more than 85 characters, including spaces"; must be provided as a Word document; "select 'Highlights' from the drop-down list when uploading files".

=====================================================================
6. REFERENCE STYLE — AUTHOR-YEAR, APA 7th EDITION. YES, APA.
=====================================================================
Verbatim ("Reference style"):
"Citations in the text should follow the referencing style used by the American Psychological Association. You are referred to the Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association, Seventh Edition (2020) ISBN 978-1-4338-3215-4.
The reference list should be arranged alphabetically and then chronologically. More than one reference from the same author(s) in the same year must be identified by the letters 'a', 'b', 'c', etc., placed after the year of publication."

=> AUTHOR-YEAR (Harvard/APA), NOT numbered. Neural Networks DOES use APA style (7th ed., 2020).
=> Reference list: alphabetical, then chronological; a/b/c suffixes for same author(s) + same year.
=> IMPORTANT: the Guide names NO .bst file. The APA/author-year requirement maps to:
   - CAS templates (what the journal links to): \bibliographystyle{cas-model2-names} — "cas-model2-names.bst — formats references using name-date or author-year style" (https://arxiv.org/html/2408.08109v1).
   - elsarticle: \documentclass[...,authoryear]{elsarticle} with \bibliographystyle{elsarticle-harv} ("elsarticle-harv.bst — for author-year referencing"), per elsdoc (https://ctan.math.washington.edu/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/elsarticle/doc/elsdoc.tex).
   Do NOT use elsarticle-num.bst / model1-num-names.bst for this journal.

Verbatim worked examples given in the guide:
- Journal: "Van der Geer, J., Handgraaf T., & Lupton, R. A. (2020). The art of writing a scientific article. Journal of Scientific Communications, 163, 51–59. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.sc.2020.00372."
- Journal with article number: "Van der Geer, J., Handgraaf, T., & Lupton, R. A. (2022). The art of writing a scientific article. Heliyon, 19, Article e00205. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heliyon.2022.e00205."
- Book: "Strunk, W., Jr., & White, E. B. (2000). The elements of style (4th ed.). Longman (Chapter 4)."
- Book chapter: "Mettam, G. R., & Adams, L. B. (2020). How to prepare an electronic version of your article. In B. S. Jones, & R. Z. Smith (Eds.), Introduction to the electronic age (pp. 281–304). E-Publishing Inc."
- Website: "Powertech Systems. (2022). Lithium-ion vs lead-acid cost analysis. Retrieved from http://www.powertechsystems.eu/home/tech-corner/lithium-ion-vs-lead-acid-cost-analysis/. Accessed January 6, 2022."
- Dataset: "Oguro, M., Imahiro, S., Saito, S., & Nakashizuka, T. (2015). Mortality data for Japanese oak wilt disease and surrounding forest compositions [dataset]. Mendeley Data, v1. https://doi.org/10.17632/xwj98nb39r.1."
- Conference/poster: "Engle, E.K., Cash, T.F., & Jarry, J.L. (2019, November). The Body Image Behaviours Inventory-3: Development and validation of the Body Image Compulsive Actions and Body Image Avoidance Scales. Poster session presentation at the meeting of the Association for Behavioural and Cognitive Therapies, New York, NY."
- Software: "Coon, E., Berndt, M., ... & Molins, S. (2020). Advanced Terrestrial Simulator (ATS) (Version 0.88) [Computer software]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3727209."

Other reference rules (verbatim highlights):
"Any references cited within your article should also be present in your reference list and vice versa."
"We recommend that you do not include unpublished results and personal communications in your reference list, though you may mention them in the text of your article." / "In substitution of the publication date add "unpublished results" or "personal communication.""
"References cited as "in press" imply that the item has been accepted for publication."
Datasets: "Add [dataset] immediately before your reference. This will help us to properly identify the dataset. The [dataset] identifier will not appear in your published article."
Preprints: "We ask you to mark preprints clearly. You should include the word "preprint" or the name of the preprint server as part of your reference and provide the preprint DOI. Where a preprint has subsequently become available as a peer-reviewed publication, use the formal publication as your reference."
Reference managers: "We advise you to remove all field codes before submitting your manuscript to any reference management software product."

=====================================================================
7. LaTeX — THE JOURNAL LINKS THE **CAS** TEMPLATE, NOT elsarticle
=====================================================================
Verbatim (Guide, "LaTeX"):
"We encourage you use our LaTeX template when preparing a LaTeX submission. You will be asked to provide all relevant editable source files upon submission or revision.
Support for your LaTeX submission:
LaTeX submission instructions and templates
Journal Article Publishing Support Center LaTeX FAQs and support
Researcher Academy's Beginners' guide to writing a manuscript in LaTeX"

CRITICAL DETAIL FOUND BY INSPECTING THE PAGE'S LINK TARGETS: the words "LaTeX template" hyperlink to
https://assets.ctfassets.net/o78em1y1w4i4/5uFmLZJTPDMAUjFnHRpjj8/6f19a979146eb93263763d87a894ab0d/els-cas-templates.zip
i.e. the Elsevier **CAS (Complex Article Service) template package**, which provides cas-sc.cls (single column) and cas-dc.cls (double column) — NOT elsarticle.cls. "LaTeX submission instructions and templates" links to https://www.elsevier.com/latex.

So, answering precisely:
- Is elsarticle.cls "the recommended class"? Not exactly. Elsevier's generic /latex page still presents elsarticle as its article class ("elsarticle" + "elsarticle-num.bst ... a BibTeX style file for the numbered reference style"), but the Neural Networks Guide's own "LaTeX template" download is the CAS bundle (cas-sc.cls / cas-dc.cls). Both are accepted by Elsevier's system; CAS is what this journal hands you.
- There is NO Neural-Networks-specific LaTeX template or .cls. Nothing on the page names one.
- CAS usage (https://arxiv.org/html/2408.08109v1): "\documentclass[<options>]{cas-sc}" for single column, "\documentclass[<options>]{cas-dc}" for two column; option `longmktitle` documented for long front matter; bibliography via \bibliographystyle{cas-model2-names} (author-year, correct for this journal) or \bibliographystyle{model1-num-names} (numbered, wrong for this journal). "Authors are requested to choose any one of these according to the journal style." Class files "are now accepted for submitting articles both in Elsevier's electronic submission system and elsewhere."
- elsarticle.cls options, if you use elsarticle instead (verbatim option list from elsdoc, https://ctan.math.washington.edu/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/elsarticle/doc/elsdoc.tex): `preprint` (default; formats for submission to Elsevier journals), `review` (like preprint but increases the baselineskip to facilitate easier review), `1p` (model 1+ look, always single column), `3p` (model 3+ look; combine with `twocolumn` for two-column models), `5p` (model 5+ look, always two column), `times` (loads txfonts/Times), `authoryear` (author-year citation style of natbib), `number`, `sort&compress`, `longtitle`, `reversenotenum`, `lefttitle`, `endfloat`, `nonatbib`, `doubleblind`, `twocolumn`. Usage: `\documentclass[<options>]{elsarticle}`; a typical final-form line is `\documentclass[final,1p,times,authoryear]{elsarticle}`.
  For Neural Networks the correct elsarticle combination is the AUTHORYEAR one, e.g. `\documentclass[preprint,12pt,authoryear]{elsarticle}` + `\bibliographystyle{elsarticle-harv}`. Do NOT use `doubleblind` (see item 1) and do NOT use `number`/elsarticle-num.bst.
- CAS bundle scope (CTAN): "The els-cas-templates bundle provides two classfiles, namely cas-sc.cls and cas-dc.cls and corresponding template files... cas-sc.cls is meant for one-column, while cas-dc.cls is for two-column layout."

File-format rules that constrain LaTeX/Word choice (verbatim, "File format"):
"We ask you to provide editable source files for your entire submission (including figures, tables and text graphics). Some guidelines:
Save files in an editable format, using the extension .doc/.docx for Word files and .tex for LaTeX files. A PDF is not an acceptable source file.
Format Word files in a single-column layout. Double-column formatting is only permitted for LaTeX submissions.
Remove any strikethrough and underlined text from your manuscript, unless it has scientific significance related to your article.
Use spell-check and grammar-check functions to avoid errors."
=> NOTE: a PDF is NOT an acceptable source file; Word must be SINGLE column; only LaTeX may be double column.
And ("Submit online"): "The system converts your article files to a single PDF file used in the peer-review process. Editable files (e.g., Word, LaTeX) are required to typeset your article for final publication."

=====================================================================
8. REQUIRED DECLARATIONS AND SEPARATE FILES
=====================================================================
COVER LETTER — NOT MENTIONED. The word "cover letter" does not appear anywhere in the Guide for Authors (I grepped the full retrieved text). No cover letter is required by the guide; the submission system may still offer an optional "Comments to the Editor" box.

DECLARATION OF INTEREST / COMPETING INTERESTS — REQUIRED, SEPARATE UPLOADED WORD FILE, GENERATED BY A TOOL. Verbatim:
"All authors must disclose any financial and personal relationships with other people or organizations that could inappropriately influence or bias their work. Examples of potential competing interests include: Employment / Consultancies / Stock ownership / Honoraria / Paid expert testimony / Patent applications or registrations / Grants or any other funding / Affiliation with the journal as an Editor or Advisory Board Member
The declarations tool should always be completed.
Authors with a journal affiliation to declare should enter the following text under "Other Activities" within the declarations tool and should inform the journal and publisher prior to completing the submission process:
Given their role as [AUTHOR JOURNAL ROLE TITLE], [AUTHOR NAME] had no involvement in the peer-review of this article and has no access to information regarding its peer-review. Full responsibility for the editorial process for this article was delegated to another journal editor.
Editorial disclosure statements will be included as a footnote and/or in the declaration of competing interest section of the article.
Authors with no competing interests to declare should select the option "I have nothing to declare".
The resulting Word document containing your declaration should be uploaded at the "attach/upload files" step in the submission process. It is important that the Word document is saved in the .doc/.docx file format. Author signatures are not required."
The "declarations tool" links to https://declarations.elsevier.com/ .
=> ACTION: run the declarations tool, download the generated .doc/.docx, upload it as a separate file. Signatures NOT needed.

CRediT AUTHOR STATEMENT — REQUIRED. Verbatim:
"Corresponding authors are required to acknowledge co-author contributions using CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy) roles:
Conceptualization / Data curation / Formal analysis / Funding acquisition / Investigation / Methodology / Project administration / Resources / Software / Supervision / Validation / Visualization / Writing – original draft / Writing – review and editing
Not all CRediT roles will apply to every manuscript and some authors may contribute through multiple roles."
Elsevier's CRediT page (https://www.elsevier.com/researcher/author/policies-and-guidelines/credit-author-statement): statements "should be provided during the submission process and will appear above the acknowledgment section of the published paper." Example given there: "Zhang San: Conceptualization, Methodology, Software. Priya Singh: Data Curation, Writing - Original Draft. Wang Wu: Visualization, Investigation. Jan Jansen: Supervision. Ajay Kumar: Software, Validation. Sun Qi: Writing - Review & Editing."

DATA AVAILABILITY / RESEARCH DATA — OPTION C, DEPOSIT IS REQUIRED. Verbatim:
"For this journal, Option C instructions from our research data guidelines apply. This means that you are required to:
Deposit your research data in a relevant data repository.
Cite and link to this dataset in your article.
If this is not possible, make a statement explaining why research data cannot be shared."
Also: "Provide a link to your dataset when prompted during the online submission process." and identifier format "Database: 12345 (e.g. TAIR: AT1G01020; CCDC: 734053; PDB: 1XFN)."
=> This is one of the stricter Elsevier tiers: data deposit + citation is mandatory unless you justify why not.

FUNDING STATEMENT — REQUIRED. Verbatim:
"Authors must disclose any funding sources who provided financial support for the conduct of the research and/or preparation of the article. The role of sponsors, if any, should be declared in relation to the study design, collection, analysis and interpretation of data, writing of the report and decision to submit the article for publication. If funding sources had no such involvement this should be stated in your submission.
List funding sources in this standard way to facilitate compliance to funder's requirements:
Funding: This work was supported by the National Institutes of Health [grant numbers xxxx, yyyy]; the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Seattle, WA [grant number zzzz]; and the United States Institutes of Peace [grant number aaaa].
It is not necessary to include detailed descriptions on the program or type of grants, scholarships and awards. When funding is from a block grant or other resources available to a university, college, or other research institution, submit the name of the institute or organization that provided the funding.
If no funding has been provided for the research, it is recommended to include the following sentence:
This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors."

ETHICS STATEMENT — no separate ethics-statement file is mandated by this guide; the requirement is compliance. Verbatim ("Ethics in publishing"): "Authors must follow ethical guidelines stated in Elsevier's Publishing Ethics Policy."
Related, verbatim ("Submission declaration"):
"When authors submit an article to an Elsevier journal it is implied that:
The work described has not been published previously except in the form of a preprint, an abstract, a published lecture, academic thesis or registered report. See our policy on multiple, redundant or concurrent publication.
The article is not under consideration for publication elsewhere.
The article's publication is approved by all authors and tacitly or explicitly by the responsible authorities where the work was carried out.
If accepted, the article will not be published elsewhere in the same form, in English or in any other language, including electronically, without the written consent of the copyright-holder.
To verify compliance with our journal publishing policies, we may check your manuscript with our screening tools."
Authorship criteria (verbatim): "All authors should have made substantial contributions to all of the following: The conception and design of the study, or acquisition of data, or analysis and interpretation of data / Drafting the article or revising it critically for important intellectual content. / Final approval of the version to be submitted."
Authorship changes (verbatim, strict): "The editors of this journal generally will not consider changes to authorship once a manuscript has been submitted... Changes can only be made prior to acceptance, and only if approved by the journal editor... Requests to change authorship must be made by the corresponding author using the Authorship Change Request form... This journal does not allow authorship changes after acceptance."
SAGER: "Sex and gender-based analyses (SGBA) should be integrated into research design when research involves or pertains to humans, animals or eukaryotic cells."

DECLARATION OF GENERATIVE AI USE — REQUIRED IF USED; NEW SECTION BEFORE THE REFERENCES. Verbatim:
"Authors must declare the use of generative AI tools in the manuscript preparation process upon submission of the paper."
"The use of AI tools in the manuscript preparation process must be declared by adding a statement at the end of the manuscript when the paper is first submitted. The statement will appear in the published work and should be placed in a new section before the references list. An example:
Title of new section: Declaration of generative AI and AI-assisted technologies in the manuscript preparation process.
Statement: During the preparation of this work the author(s) used [NAME OF TOOL / SERVICE] in order to [REASON]. After using this tool/service, the author(s) reviewed and edited the content as needed and take(s) full responsibility for the content of the published article."
"The declaration does not apply to the use of basic tools, such as tools used to check grammar, spelling and references. In addition, authors are not required to disclose the use of AI tools or features within specialist disability-related assistive technology, provided these are used solely for accessibility purposes.
If you have nothing to disclose, you do not need to add a statement."
"authors must not list or cite AI tools as an author or co-author on the manuscript since authorship implies responsibilities and tasks that can only be attributed to, and performed by, humans."
"this journal does not currently allow academic editors and reviewers to upload an unpublished manuscript into a generative AI tool".

ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS (separate section, placement rule) — verbatim:
"Include any individuals who provided you with help during your research, such as help with language, writing or proof reading, in the acknowledgements section.
Acknowledgements should be placed in a separate section which appears directly before the reference list. Do not include acknowledgements on your title page, as a footnote to your title, or anywhere else in your article other than in the separate acknowledgements section."
=> Back-matter order implied: Acknowledgements → GenAI declaration section → References. (Both are specified as immediately before the reference list; put the GenAI section last before References.)

SEPARATE FILES SUMMARY: (i) manuscript source (.docx or .tex, editable, PDF not acceptable); (ii) each figure as its own file; (iii) highlights file (optional, filename contains "highlights"); (iv) declarations-tool .doc/.docx competing-interests file; (v) supplementary material; (vi) optional Data in Brief / MethodsX co-submission.

=====================================================================
9. FIGURES / ARTWORK
=====================================================================
Verbatim:
"Figures, images, diagrams and other graphical media (artwork) must be supplied as separate files along with the manuscript, in line with these artwork and media instructions. Some excerpts:
When submitting artwork:
Cite all images in the manuscript text.
Number images according to the order they appear within your article.
Submit each image as a separate file using a logical naming convention for your files (for example, Figure_1, Figure_2 etc).
Text graphics may be embedded in the text at the appropriate position. If you are working with LaTeX, text graphics may also be embedded in the file."

Captions (verbatim): "All artwork must have a caption. A caption should consist of a brief title (not displayed on the figure itself) and a description of the image. Keep the amount of text in any image to a minimum, though any symbol or abbreviation should be explained."

Formats and resolution (verbatim):
"When your artwork is finalized, "save as" or convert your electronic artwork to the formats listed below taking into account the given resolution requirements for line drawings, halftones, and line/halftone combinations:
Vector drawings: Save as EPS or PDF files embedding the font or saving the text as "graphics."
Color or grayscale photographs (halftones): Save as TIFF, JPG or PNG files using a minimum of 300 dpi (for single column width: min. 1063 pixels, full page width: 2244 pixels).
Bitmapped line drawings: Save as TIFF, JPG or PNG files, using a minimum of 1000 dpi (for single column width: min. 3543 pixels, full page width: 7480 pixels).
Combinations bitmapped line/halftones (color or grayscale): Save as TIFF, JPG or PNG files using a minimum of 500 dpi (for single column: min. 1772 pixels, full page width: 3740 pixels).
Please do not submit:
Files that are too low in resolution.
Artwork where text is disproportionately small compared to the image size, as text may become unreadable.
Different images or graphs combined into one, as this affects accessibility"

COLOUR POLICY (verbatim): "If you submit usable color figures with your accepted article, we will ensure that they appear in color online.
Please ensure that color images are accessible to all, including those with impaired color vision. Learn more about color and web accessibility."
=> Colour online is free/automatic; the guide states NO colour-in-print charge and mentions no print colour fee at all.

GENERATIVE AI IN FIGURES (verbatim excerpt of the policy reproduced in the guide):
"AI tools may be used to support the creation of explanatory images (such as flow charts, conceptual diagrams, or schematic illustrations)
AI tools may be used to create data visualizations (such as plots, charts, graphs, or heatmaps) when the output is directly derived from underlying data using reproducible analytical, computational, or statistical methods.
AI tools must not be used to create or alter images that represent primary observed or experimental data... This includes adjustments to brightness, contrast, or color balance, which should only be done using established image processing software."
"If you used generative AI tools to create images in your manuscript, you should disclose this in each image caption as well as in the general Generative AI disclosure statement."

TABLES (verbatim): "Tables must be submitted as editable text, not as images... Place tables next to the relevant text or on a separate page(s) at the end of your article. Cite all tables in the manuscript text. Number tables consecutively according to their appearance in the text. Please provide captions along with the tables. Place any table notes below the table body. Avoid vertical rules and shading within table cells."

MATH (verbatim): "Submit math equations as editable text, not as images. Present simple formulae in line with normal text, where possible. Use the solidus (/) instead of a horizontal line for small fractional terms such as X/Y. Present variables in italics. Denote powers of e by exp. Display equations separately from your text, numbering them consecutively in the order they are referred to within your text."

=====================================================================
10. LINE NUMBERS / DOUBLE SPACING — NO REQUIREMENT
=====================================================================
There is NO requirement for line numbers and NO requirement for double spacing. I searched the complete retrieved text of the Guide for "line number", "double spac", "double-spac" and found zero occurrences. The only formatting mandates on layout are the File format ones quoted in item 7 (editable source; Word single-column; double-column only for LaTeX; no strikethrough/underline).
Optional aid: elsarticle's `review` option "increases the baselineskip to facilitate easier review process" if you want looser spacing, but the journal does not ask for it.

=====================================================================
11. SUBMISSION SYSTEM AND GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT
=====================================================================
SUBMISSION SYSTEM: https://submit.elsevier.com/NEUNET (this is the target of both the "Submit your article" button and the "submit your paper" link in the Guide). It is Elsevier's submission portal running on Editorial Manager — the guide names Editorial Manager explicitly in the co-submission instructions: "on the 'Attach files' page in Editorial Manager".
Verbatim ("Submit online"): "Our online submission system guides you through the process steps of entering your manuscript details and uploading your files. The system converts your article files to a single PDF file used in the peer-review process. Editable files (e.g., Word, LaTeX) are required to typeset your article for final publication. All correspondence, including notification of the editor's decision and requests for revision, is sent by email. Please follow this link to submit your paper."

GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT: NOT REQUIRED — and not even offered. The phrase "graphical abstract" appears ZERO times in the full Guide for Authors (verified by grep over the complete retrieved text; there is no "Graphical abstract" heading in the section menu either, which runs ... Title page, Abstract, Keywords, Highlights, Math formulae, Tables, Figures...). Do not prepare one.

OTHER SUBMISSION-STAGE ITEMS WORTH KNOWING:
- Submission checklist (verbatim): "One author has been designated as the corresponding author and their full contact details (email address, full postal address, and phone numbers) have been provided... All files have been uploaded, including artwork, videos, and supplementary materials. Don't forget to include tables and footnotes in the files, and to submit captions. checks.uncertainties:
1. ScienceDirect blocks server-side fetching (HTTP 403), so the Guide for Authors was read through a rendered browser session rather than a plain HTTP fetch. The extracted text is the page's <main> element and appears complete (it spans Aims and scope through Author support and matches the page's own section menu), but I could not diff it against the "Print Guide as PDF" version. If absolute certainty is needed on any single clause, regenerate the PDF from the page's "Print Guide as PDF" control.

2. LENGTH LIMIT FOR FULL ARTICLES — NOT FOUND. The current guide states no page, word, or reference limit for regular Articles; the only limits given are for Letters (2500 words / 100-word abstract / 25 refs / figures+tables ≤1 page) and Letters to the Editor (≤2 formatted pages). Older third-party summaries of this journal sometimes cite page limits; none appear in the live guide. Treat "no stated limit" as the current position, but note that an editor could still impose one editorially.

3. elsarticle vs CAS. The Neural Networks guide says only "We encourage you use our LaTeX template" without naming a class; I resolved the actual hyperlink in the page DOM, which points to els-cas-templates.zip (CAS: cas-sc.cls / cas-dc.cls). Elsevier's generic /latex page still foregrounds elsarticle. So elsarticle.cls is accepted but is NOT what this journal's own template link delivers. There is no Neural-Networks-specific .cls or template — I found no evidence of one on the journal page or in the CAS/elsarticle bundles.

4. No .bst is named anywhere by the journal. The mapping I give (cas-model2-names.bst for CAS; elsarticle-harv.bst + authoryear for elsarticle) is my inference from the journal's explicit APA-7 author-year requirement combined with the class documentation. It is the correct mapping, but the journal never states a .bst filename, so a production editor could restyle.

5. The elsarticle class-option list came from the elsdoc.tex source read through a summarizing fetch rather than from the compiled elsdoc.pdf. The options named (preprint, review, 1p, 3p, 5p, times, twocolumn, authoryear, number, sort&compress, longtitle, reversenotenum, lefttitle, endfloat, nonatbib, doubleblind) are as reported from that source; exact spelling of the rarer ones (e.g. `sort&compress`, `reversenotenum`) should be confirmed against the compiled elsdoc.pdf before use. The CAS option list is thinner — only `longmktitle` was explicitly documented in the arXiv CAS documentation I read; other CAS options exist in the .cls but were not enumerated on the pages I fetched.

6. Data availability statement wording. The journal applies "Option C" (deposit required), but neither the journal page nor Elsevier's data-guidelines page supplies a mandatory sentence template for the Data Availability Statement. In practice Editorial Manager prompts for one at submission and generates the published statement; I could not see that in-system prompt without logging in.

7. Cover letter: I am confident it is not required by the guide (zero occurrences of "cover letter" in the full text), but submission systems commonly expose an optional "Comments to the Editor" field or an optional cover-letter upload slot that is not documented in the guide. I could not inspect submit.elsevier.com/NEUNET's actual upload item list without authenticating.

8. Graphical abstract: confidently NOT required and not offered (zero occurrences in the full guide, and absent from the section menu, unlike many other Elsevier journals which have a dedicated "Graphical abstract" heading). Small residual risk that the submission system still exposes an optional item type for it.

9. Line numbers / double spacing: confidently not required (zero occurrences of "line number", "double spac", "double-spac"). Some Elsevier journals request line numbering only in the reviewer PDF; Neural Networks does not.

10. Society affiliation: the task brief said INNS/ENNS/JNNS. The live guide says INNS, APNNS (Asia-Pacific Neural Network Society), and JNNS. ENNS is not listed in the current text. I did not investigate when or whether ENNS was dropped.

11. Article Processing Charge amount for the open-access option is not stated on the guide page (it links out to an open-access information page I did not fetch, since it was out of scope for the eleven questions).

checks.findings:
All items below were verified by fetching live Elsevier-owned pages on 2026-08-11. The single most authoritative source for a Neural Networks submission is the journal's own Guide for Authors, which now lives on ScienceDirect (elsevier.com/journals/neural-networks/0893-6080/guide-for-authors issues a 301 to it). WebFetch is blocked (403) on that host, so I read it with the browser tool; the full extracted text is saved at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Volumes-Crucial-X6-MacBook-Code-ml-papers/86fbc9c4-7358-4aff-9451-5f33ce107df2/scratchpad/nn_gfa.txt

IMPORTANT HEADLINE CHANGE (affects Q2): Elsevier has renamed the AI declaration. The current wording everywhere that matters for Neural Networks is "Declaration of generative AI and AI-assisted technologies in the MANUSCRIPT PREPARATION process" — not "...in the writing process". The old "writing process" phrasing survives only on a legacy publishing-ethics page. Use the new name.

=====================================================================
1. DECLARATION OF COMPETING INTEREST — WORDING WHEN THERE IS NONE
=====================================================================
Elsevier's official Declaration of Interest Statement template (.docx, linked from Elsevier support and the Declaration Tool) offers three tick-box options. The "none" option reads verbatim:

  "The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper."

The other two options in the same template are, verbatim:

  "The author is an Editorial Board Member/Editor-in-Chief/Associate Editor/Guest Editor for this journal and was not involved in the editorial review or the decision to publish this article."

  "The authors declare the following financial interests/personal relationships which may be considered as potential competing interests:"

(A variant of the same template heads the block "Declaration of interests" and reads "...for [Journal name]..." in the editor option. Some journals substitute "in this article" for "in this paper"; the canonical template says "in this paper".)

What the Neural Networks guide itself says (verbatim extracts):
  - "All authors must disclose any financial and personal relationships with other people or organizations that could inappropriately influence or bias their work."
  - Listed examples: "Employment / Consultancies / Stock ownership / Honoraria / Paid expert testimony / Patent applications or registrations / Grants or any other funding / Affiliation with the journal as an Editor or Advisory Board Member"
  - "The declarations tool should always be completed."
  - "Authors with no competing interests to declare should select the option \"I have nothing to declare\"."
  - Editor/board-member authors must paste this verbatim under "Other Activities" in the declarations tool: "Given their role as [AUTHOR JOURNAL ROLE TITLE], [AUTHOR NAME] had no involvement in the peer-review of this article and has no access to information regarding its peer-review. Full responsibility for the editorial process for this article was delegated to another journal editor."
  - "Editorial disclosure statements will be included as a footnote and/or in the declaration of competing interest section of the article."

Related, same section of the guide — FUNDING (verbatim):
  - Format: "Funding: This work was supported by the National Institutes of Health [grant numbers xxxx, yyyy]; the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Seattle, WA [grant number zzzz]; and the United States Institutes of Peace [grant number aaaa]."
  - If unfunded: "This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors."

=====================================================================
2. DECLARATION OF GENERATIVE AI — WORDING AND PLACEMENT
=====================================================================
CURRENT wording, from the Neural Networks Guide for Authors and confirmed on Elsevier's "Generative AI policies for journals" page. The guide gives the example as a titled pair, verbatim:

  Title of new section: "Declaration of generative AI and AI-assisted technologies in the manuscript preparation process."
  Statement: "During the preparation of this work the author(s) used [NAME OF TOOL / SERVICE] in order to [REASON]. After using this tool/service, the author(s) reviewed and edited the content as needed and take(s) full responsibility for the content of the published article."

(The policy page renders the first clause with a comma — "During the preparation of this work, the author(s) used..." — the journal guide has no comma. Either is fine; I'd match the journal guide.)

PLACEMENT (verbatim from the NN guide): "The use of AI tools in the manuscript preparation process must be declared by adding a statement at the end of the manuscript when the paper is first submitted. The statement will appear in the published work and should be placed in a new section before the references list."
The GenAI policies page phrases placement as "at the end of your manuscript, immediately before the references."
So: end of the main manuscript file, as its own numbered/unnumbered section immediately before the reference list, present at first submission (not added later).

WHEN NO DECLARATION IS NEEDED (verbatim from the NN guide): "The declaration does not apply to the use of basic tools, such as tools used to check grammar, spelling and references. In addition, authors are not required to disclose the use of AI tools or features within specialist disability-related assistive technology, provided these are used solely for accessibility purposes." and "If you have nothing to disclose, you do not need to add a statement."

OTHER BINDING AI RULES for a Neural Networks submission (verbatim from the guide):
  - "authors must not list or cite AI tools as an author or co-author on the manuscript since authorship implies responsibilities and tasks that can only be attributed to, and performed by, humans."
  - Figures: "AI tools may be used to support the creation of explanatory images (such as flow charts, conceptual diagrams, or schematic illustrations)"; "AI tools may be used to create data visualizations (such as plots, charts, graphs, or heatmaps) when the output is directly derived from underlying data using reproducible analytical, computational, or statistical methods."; "AI tools must not be used to create or alter images that represent primary observed or experimental data..."
  - "If you used generative AI tools to create images in your manuscript, you should disclose this in each image caption as well as in the general Generative AI disclosure statement."
  - Note for a Neural Networks paper specifically: AI used as part of the research itself (i.e. your models) is not what this declaration covers — that belongs in the methods; the policy "does not prevent the use of AI tools in formal research design or research methods".
  - Reviewers/editors on this journal may not upload unpublished manuscripts into generative AI tools.

=====================================================================
3. CREDIT — THE 14 ROLES AND STATEMENT FORMAT
=====================================================================
The Neural Networks guide states verbatim: "Corresponding authors are required to acknowledge co-author contributions using CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy) roles:" and lists exactly 14, in this order and spelling:

  1. Conceptualization
  2. Data curation
  3. Formal analysis
  4. Funding acquisition
  5. Investigation
  6. Methodology
  7. Project administration
  8. Resources
  9. Software
  10. Supervision
  11. Validation
  12. Visualization
  13. Writing – original draft
  14. Writing – review and editing

(Elsevier's CRediT reference page styles the last two as "Writing - Original Draft" and "Writing - Review & Editing". The journal guide's rendering — en dash, "and editing" — is the one to match for this journal. Elsevier's statement-templates file uses a third rendering, "Writing–original draft" / "Writing–review & editing". The role set is identical in all three.)

Guide also states verbatim: "Not all CRediT roles will apply to every manuscript and some authors may contribute through multiple roles."

Official role definitions (verbatim, from Elsevier's CRediT author statement page):
  Conceptualization — "Ideas; formulation or evolution of overarching research goals and aims"
  Methodology — "Development or design of methodology; creation of models"
  Software — "Programming, software development; designing computer programs; implementation of the computer code and supporting algorithms; testing of existing code components"
  Validation — "Verification, whether as a part of the activity or separate, of the overall replication/ reproducibility of results/experiments and other research outputs"
  Formal analysis — "Application of statistical, mathematical, computational, or other formal techniques to analyze or synthesize study data"
  Investigation — "Conducting a research and investigation process, specifically performing the experiments, or data/evidence collection"
  Resources — "Provision of study materials, reagents, materials, patients, laboratory samples, animals, instrumentation, computing resources, or other analysis tools"
  Data Curation — "Management activities to annotate (produce metadata), scrub data and maintain research data"
  Writing - Original Draft — "Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically writing the initial draft"
  Writing - Review & Editing — "Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work by those from the original research group, specifically critical review, commentary or revision"
  Visualization — "Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically visualization/ data presentation"
  Supervision — "Oversight and leadership responsibility for the research activity planning and execution, including mentorship external to the core team"
  Project administration — "Management and coordination responsibility for the research activity planning and execution"
  Funding acquisition — "Acquisition of the financial support for the project leading to this publication"

FORMAT: author name, colon, comma-separated roles, full stop; repeat per author. Elsevier's official example, verbatim:
  "Zhang San: Conceptualization, Methodology, Software. Priya Singh: Data Curation, Writing - Original Draft. Wang Wu: Visualization, Investigation. Jan Jansen: Supervision. Ajay Kumar: Software, Validation. Sun Qi: Writing - Review & Editing."

WHERE IT GOES: Elsevier's CRediT page states "CRediT statements should be provided during the submission process and will appear above the acknowledgment section of the published paper." So it is entered in the submission system (Editorial Manager) rather than being a mandatory manuscript section, and Elsevier renders it above Acknowledgements. Including a matching "CRediT authorship contribution statement" section in the manuscript just before Acknowledgements is standard practice and harmless.

=====================================================================
4. DATA AVAILABILITY
=====================================================================
Neural Networks is an Option C journal. Verbatim from the guide: "For this journal, Option C instructions from our research data guidelines apply. This means that you are required to: Deposit your research data in a relevant data repository. Cite and link to this dataset in your article. If this is not possible, make a statement explaining why research data cannot be shared."

Elsevier's definition of research data explicitly includes code (verbatim): "Research data refers to the results of observations or experimentation that validate research findings, which may also include software, code, models, algorithms, protocols, methods and other useful materials related to the project." — so a GitHub/Zenodo code release counts.

Elsevier's official statement templates (Statement_templates.docx, hosted by Elsevier) give these options with verbatim wording:
  - Data openly available in a public repository that issues datasets with DOIs: "The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in [repository name e.g "figshare"] at http://doi.org/[doi], reference number [reference number]."
  - Data openly available in a public repository that does not issue DOIs: "The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in [repository name] at [URL], reference number [reference number]."
  - Data derived from public domain resources: "The data that support the findings of this study are available in [repository name] at [URL/DOI], reference number [reference number]. These data were derived from the following resources available in the public domain: [list resources and URLs]"
  - Embargo on data due to commercial restrictions: "The data that support the findings will be available in [repository name] at [URL / DOI link] following an embargo from the date of publication to allow for commercialization of research findings."
  - Data available on request due to privacy/ethical restrictions: "The data that support the findings of this study are available on request from the corresponding author. The data are not publicly available due to privacy or ethical restrictions."
  - Data subject to third party restrictions: "The data that support the findings of this study are available from [third party]. Restrictions apply to the availability of these data, which were used under license for this study. Data are available [from the authors / at URL] with the permission of [third party]."
  - Data available on request from the authors: "The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request."
  - Data sharing not applicable – no new data generated: "Data sharing is not applicable to this article as no new data were created or analyzed in this study."
  - Author elects to not share data: "Research data are not shared."
  - Data available in article supplementary material: "The data that supports the findings of this study are available in the supplementary material of this article"
  - No new data / entirely theoretical research: "Data sharing not applicable to this article as no datasets were generated or analysed during the current study"

RECOMMENDED WORDING FOR CODE + DATA IN A PUBLIC REPO (GitHub/Zenodo): use the DOI variant, since Zenodo mints DOIs and GitHub alone does not. Zenodo -> DOI template; GitHub-only -> URL template. See exact_template_text for the fill-in versions.

Elsevier Author Services additionally offers this shorter phrasing for the shareable case: "The raw data required to reproduce the above findings are available to download from [INSERT PERMANENT WEB LINK(s)]." Elsevier also notes there are no restrictions on which repository you choose, and that the DAS sits "right before the reference section".

Practical note: the data availability statement is generally captured in the Editorial Manager submission flow ("The majority of Elsevier journals will have integrated the option to create data statement directly in the submission flow") and is published "under the 'research data' section from the article outline". Also link the dataset via the guide's data-linking route: "Provide a link to your dataset when prompted during the online submission process."

=====================================================================
5. SEPARATE FILE OR IN THE MANUSCRIPT?
=====================================================================
For Neural Networks: SEPARATE FILE, generated by Elsevier's Declaration Tool. Verbatim from the guide: "The declarations tool should always be completed." ... "The resulting Word document containing your declaration should be uploaded at the \"attach/upload files\" step in the submission process. It is important that the Word document is saved in the .doc/.docx file format. Author signatures are not required."

So the workflow is: go to declarations.elsevier.com, complete the four disclosure categories (Reported Work / Outside this Work / Intellectual Property / Other Activities) or select "I have nothing to declare", download the produced .doc/.docx, and upload it as a separate submission item. Do not convert it to PDF; no signatures needed.

The current guide does NOT require a competing-interest paragraph inside the manuscript file — it says nothing about one. The published article still carries a "Declaration of competing interest" section (the guide references "the declaration of competing interest section of the article"), which Elsevier populates from the tool. Including the one-line statement in your manuscript before the references anyway is common and safe, and it is what appears in the published record; it just does not substitute for uploading the tool's file.

Note: the older Elsevier boilerplate that told authors to put "Declarations of interest: none" in the title page/manuscript AND submit a separate form has been superseded on this journal's current guide — the declarations tool file is now the mechanism. Do not use the "Declarations of interest: none" phrasing as your only compliance step.

=====================================================================
SUGGESTED SECTION ORDER AT THE END OF THE MANUSCRIPT
=====================================================================
Based on the guide's placement rules (acknowledgements "directly before the reference list"; AI declaration "in a new section before the references list"; CRediT rendered "above the acknowledgment section"):
  ... Conclusion -> CRediT authorship contribution statement -> Declaration of competing interest -> Declaration of generative AI and AI-assisted technologies in the manuscript preparation process -> Acknowledgements -> Funding -> Data availability -> References
(Exact interleaving of the last few is handled by Elsevier at typesetting; the hard constraints are that Acknowledgements and the AI declaration both sit immediately before the references, and CRediT sits above Acknowledgements.)

checks.uncertainties:
1. Section-name drift on the AI declaration. Elsevier's current pages (the Neural Networks guide and the GenAI policies for journals page) both say "manuscript preparation process"; the older publishing-ethics page still says "writing process", which is what the question asked for. I could not find a redirect or deprecation notice reconciling the two, so both are live on elsevier.com simultaneously. I recommend the "manuscript preparation process" title because it is what the journal's own guide prints, but an editor working from the old page may expect the other. Low risk either way.

2. Punctuation variants in the AI statement. Journal guide: "During the preparation of this work the author(s) used..." (no comma). GenAI policy page: "During the preparation of this work, the author(s) used..." (comma). Same sentence otherwise. I could not determine which is the intended canonical form.

3. CRediT role-name typography differs across three Elsevier sources (journal guide: "Writing – original draft" / "Writing – review and editing"; CRediT page: "Writing - Original Draft" / "Writing - Review & Editing"; statement-templates file: "Writing–original draft" / "Writing–review & editing"). The 14 roles are identical; only capitalization, dash type, and "and" vs "&" vary. I used the journal guide's form in the paste-ready template.

4. "in this paper" vs "in this article" in the competing-interest sentence. The official .docx template says "in this paper". Many published Elsevier articles use "in this article". I could not find a page stating which is preferred; the .docx is the more authoritative source so I used "in this paper".

5. Whether Neural Networks additionally wants a competing-interest paragraph inside the manuscript file. The current guide only describes the separate uploaded declarations-tool file and never instructs authors to add in-manuscript text, yet it refers to "the declaration of competing interest section of the article" as something that exists in the published record. I could not resolve whether that section is author-supplied or Elsevier-generated at proof stage. Including it in the manuscript as well is the safe course, but the tool file upload is what the guide makes mandatory.

6. The declarations tool's exact machine-generated output for "I have nothing to declare" was not verified directly — reaching it requires stepping through and submitting a form, which I did not do. I relied on the official .docx template, which carries the same sentence and is what the tool is built around.

7. Data availability statement templates come from Elsevier-hosted files under legacyfileshare.elsevier.com rather than a current /researcher/ policy page. The live data-statement and data-guidelines pages describe Options A–E and where the statement appears, but do not themselves enumerate template sentences — they defer to the journal guide and the submission flow. The Neural Networks guide does not print a data availability template either; it only states the Option C requirement. So the verbatim templates I quote are Elsevier's official ones but are not restated on the journal's own page.

8. The Neural Networks guide has no section headed "Data availability" or "Declaration of interest" — those exact strings do not appear in it. My answers for those items are assembled from the guide's "Research data"/"Declaration of competing interests" sections plus Elsevier's corporate templates.

9. www.sciencedirect.com returns 403 to WebFetch, so the journal guide was read through the browser tool. Content was captured in full (56 KB) and I quoted directly from it, but it was not independently re-verified through a second channel.
